subject: fix(context): P10.8 — an evicted tool result must still say what it was
prompt:
The cheapest context-compaction tier destroys the only record of what it evicts. When `ContextEngine.compactWorkingSet` (packages/orchestrator/src/context-engine.ts) strips old tool-result bodies to reclaim context, it returns without calling a summarizer, so for everything it touches nothing else remembers what was there. Every evicted result becomes the same anonymous stub, "[tool result evicted to reclaim context] 15000 chars reclaimed …": a run cannot tell the read that found the bug from the one that listed a directory, and cannot judge which is worth re-running. And the size floor is so low that small results are evicted too: a 430-byte read of the spec — the file the whole task turned on — was destroyed to reclaim about 230 bytes against a stub that costs about 150.

What should happen:
- An evicted result keeps a short excerpt of its original body — its head and its tail, which is where a tool puts what matters (the path or headline at the top, the error or exit status at the bottom) — after the existing eviction marker, so it is still recognisable as an eviction. The stub stays small: well under 2,000 characters however large the original was.
- A result too small to be worth reclaiming (a few hundred bytes, e.g. a 430-byte spec read) is left untouched.
- The number of characters reported as reclaimed counts what was actually reclaimed, not the original size.

Keep the existing exported APIs working, and keep the existing tests passing.
